original_question: For a non-commutative group G, determine the invariant ν(G), the minimal number of colors required to color G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic subset A that is symmetric in the group-theoretic sense A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. In particular, decide whether ν(F_2) is finite for the free group F_2 on two generators.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.2 (R.I. Grigorchuk): investigate the invariant ν for non-commutative groups; in particular, ask whether ν(F_2) is finite, where F_2 is the free group with two generators. This problem is posed immediately after the paper defines ν(G) and after Theorem 1.1 settles the Abelian case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and the right open problem: it uses the paper’s invariant ν(G), the correct symmetry relation A = xA^{-1}x, and it singles out exactly the highlighted test case F_2 together with the finiteness question ν(F_2) < ∞. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
missing_details: The official wording is to investigate ν for non-commutative groups in general, not to promise a complete determination for an arbitrary fixed non-commutative group G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
For paper-faithfulness, ν(G) should be introduced first for an arbitrary group G and only then specialized to the non-commutative case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
To make the question fully stand-alone, it should explicitly say that a subset A ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists x ∈ G such that A = xA^{-1}x. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

The phrase “minimal number of colors” is best sharpened to the least cardinal number of colors, since Problem 1.2 then asks specifically whether this invariant is finite for F_2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

The nearby context matters: Theorem 1.1 has already computed ν(G) for Abelian groups, so Problem 1.2 is specifically the non-commutative continuation of that discussion and should not be broadened beyond it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
refined_question: Let ν(G) denote the least cardinal κ such that G admits a κ-coloring with no infinite monochromatic subset A ⊆ G satisfying A = xA^{-1}x for some x ∈ G. Investigate the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups; in particular, is ν(F_2) finite for the free group F_2 on two generators? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft. In the opening of Section 1, the paper defines ν(G) as the coloring invariant excluding infinite monochromatic symmetric subsets, then states Theorem 1.1 for Abelian groups, and immediately follows with Problem 1.2 asking for the non-commutative case, with the concrete question of whether ν(F_2) is finite. Your draft is therefore very close, but it slightly overstates the scope by saying “determine” for a non-commutative group G rather than matching the paper’s “investigate ν for non-commutative groups; in particular, is ν(F_2) finite?” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
